flashcards.front: What is the primary threat vector for Secure Web Application Design?
flashcards.back_definition: Adversaries exploit reflected user script inputs on user browser sessions to bypass standard perimeter security controls.
flashcards.back_example: Example: SAST Alert: Insecure input reflection on page profile.php
flashcards.back_confusion: Don't confuse this threat with other layers (like physical breaches or certificate revocations) which target different assets.
flashcards.back_hook: Recall: reflected user script inputs is the unlocked door; user browser sessions is what the attacker wants to steal.

flashcards.front: How does the security team mitigate Secure Web Application Design threats?
flashcards.back_definition: Deploying and enforcing context-aware HTML output encoding directly hardens user browser sessions and blocks unauthorized connections.
flashcards.back_example: Action: Update security configurations to require context-aware HTML output encoding.
flashcards.back_confusion: Don't confuse mitigation (actively blocking the exploit) with detection (simply logging or alerting the event).
flashcards.back_hook: Mitigation is the shield; detection is the security camera.

flashcards.front: How do analysts detect exploitation of Secure Web Application Design?
flashcards.back_definition: By auditing event data and implementing logic flags built to alert on SAST compiler rule checks.
flashcards.back_example: Syslog trace: SAST Alert: Insecure input reflection on page profile.php
flashcards.back_confusion: Don't confuse signature-based detection (matching known strings) with anomaly-based detection (mapping dynamic standard deviations).
flashcards.back_hook: Detection is looking for the fingerprint left behind by the threat.
